_note: Written BEFORE any reader saw a line (row IC, Session 4, the final reading). `pairs` is the approved plan's question 1 (two lines, two named marshals: which said which); `sixway` the harder test besides (IC4-R1).

pairs.line1: Sire, I need your word, and soon. I can't stand this.
pairs.line2: Perhaps you would decide, Sire. I'd rather not presume.

pairs.line1: I led the charge myself, Sire, plume and all.
pairs.line2: We struck out from my front today, Sire.

pairs.line1: I'm ready, Sire. All I lack is an enemy.
pairs.line2: Nothing to report. I've given up nothing.

pairs.line1: A quiet day, and not a gun to follow. I hate being useless.
pairs.line2: A quiet day, I'm glad to say.

pairs.line1: As you command. I'll pick up the trail again tomorrow.
pairs.line2: Fine, you're the Emperor. My task keeps.

pairs.line1: Your order first, Sire. My task is noted and will be resumed in order.
pairs.line2: As you say. Tomorrow I'm back at it, and no more delays.

pairs.line1: Called back? All right, Sire, but point me at the guns next.
pairs.line2: Recalled. The corps is closed up and ready, Sire.

pairs.line1: Give me a task, Sire, and I'll lead the assault myself.
pairs.line2: One task, Sire. I'll keep what I take and bring you more.

pairs.line1: As you command. I'll resume tomorrow, no doubt.
pairs.line2: Your order, Sire. My own chase can wait a night.

pairs.line1: One task, Sire. I'll keep what I take and bring you more.
pairs.line2: Give me a task and a few turns, Sire. I'll waste neither men nor days.

pairs.line1: Nothing to trouble you with, Sire. I'm sure you have worries enough.
pairs.line2: Nothing to do, Sire. The rolls are checked and the stores counted.

pairs.line1: Give me one task with a fight in it, Sire, and judge me by it.
pairs.line2: Give me one ride to prove myself, Sire.

rows.line: I heard guns and went, Sire. You would have done the same.
A sharp fight today, Sire. I fought it like my own ground was at stake.
I hit them hard today, Sire. I couldn't stand another day of waiting.
We charged today, Sire. A fine sight.
Every man was in place, so I sent them in, Sire.
There was fighting today, Sire. I'm sure you understand I took what care I could.
The columns marched today, Sire. I like to be near where it starts.
The men are moving, Sire. I'd have them run if I could.
Some progress today. More tomorrow, I expect.
Half the country is behind my saddle already, Sire.
The corps is on the road, flanks covered.
We advanced today. Slowly, and for good.
Consider it begun, Sire. I've waited long enough for it.
I'll check the rolls and the stores first, Sire. Then I begin.
Mounted and away, Sire.
Leave it with me, Sire. Once I have it in hand, I keep it.
Straight answer, Sire: yes. My columns are ready.
I'll do what I can, Sire, provided it's reasonable.
The job's done, Sire. Now point me at the guns.
It's finished. The cavalry is yours again.
Done. I trust it will be remembered.
The task is finished. Remember who finished it.
The task is complete, Sire. The corps is intact.
It's done, Sire, so what next? I'm no man to sit and admire it.
I stayed where I was, Sire, and it nearly killed me. Tomorrow I fight.
We stayed, Sire. I'm sure it was for the best.
I held the squadrons back, Sire. Something changed out there.
No assault today, Sire. I'll go in when the guns say so.
Things shifted, Sire, so I held. Every man is where he should be.
I did not move, Sire. This ground is mine and I don't leave it on a guess.
